title: Choose Athena Studio's multimodal direction
question: The scope is now one platform for heterogeneous data—not an image-only dashboard. These directions keep a shared project and dataset workspace while showing task-specific tools by modality. Choose one or re-roll.

options.label: Multimodal Signal Board
options.thesis: One high-clarity workspace tracks every dataset type without pretending they use the same annotation tool.
materials: amber and red for meaningful status only
options.viewport: A familiar project shell presents one sortable multimodal registry for images, video, audio/speech, text/documents, tables/time series, depth/point clouds, and custom plugins; each row names its task, source, dataset version, model state, and next action. A restrained live-status flip marks real updates, while task tools remain modality-specific.
options.risk: A departure board can feel too operational or transient; preserve durable project context, visible source/version IDs, keyboard controls, and a no-motion reduced-motion mode.

options.label: Multimodal Sample Wall
options.lineage: Streaming catalog walls and focused title cards
options.thesis: A small visible sample from each data type makes a heterogeneous workspace immediately understandable.
options.viewport: The standard dashboard shell contains rows for image, audio waveform, speech/transcript, video, tables/time-series, and custom formats; focusing a card reveals its task, label/review state, connector, and a direct route into the correct tool.
options.case: This makes unfamiliar modalities tangible for nontechnical users and communicates the shared platform better than a text-only status board.
options.risk: A media-library metaphor may overemphasize images/video; give text, audio, structured data, and custom plugins equal first-class space and keep a sortable table view.

options.label: Pixel-True Data Specimen
options.lineage: Emigre bitmap type specimens and Japanese digital publishing
options.thesis: Each modality is represented by its native shape, not by a generic file icon.
options.viewport: The normal project shell shows native previews—a thumbnail, waveform, text excerpt, time-series sparkline, or point-cloud silhouette—beside common project metadata and one action into the appropriate workflow.
options.case: Native previews help operators recognize what a dataset contains; the type-specimen treatment is less useful for scanning status across many projects.
options.risk: Low-resolution styling must never degrade actual source content or unreadable text; reserve bitmap treatment for headings and indicators.

options.label: Folded Dataset Index
options.lineage: Cassette J-cards, tracklists, and fold-out sleeves
options.thesis: A dataset carries its modality, label set, source, and version with it as a compact, readable record.
options.viewport: A shared workspace shows each dataset as a fold-out record with stable ID, modality, task, source connector, and version; audio/speech adds timeline and transcript cues, while other formats keep their own preview and tool link.
options.case: Durable records fit provenance and audio/speech timelines, but the cassette form is too specific to become the platform's universal interface.
options.risk: Do not make every modality look like an audio asset; use the fold only as a compact record treatment and retain familiar navigation.

options.label: Open Multimodal Lexicon
options.lineage: Reference lexicons with margin guides and bordered plates
options.thesis: Every unfamiliar format gets a plain-language definition, a real preview, and a direct next action.
options.viewport: A familiar dashboard shell contains a modality index with guide words and clear task names; each row explains the format in plain language and places its preview inside a bordered plate, with connector and review status in the margin.
options.case: The glossary treatment supports a genuinely broad, extensible system and helps nontechnical operators learn what each data type means.
options.risk: A reference-book metaphor can make an active workspace feel static; show current status and actions at equal visual weight to the definitions.

options.label: Synchronized Data Score
options.thesis: Time-based modalities share one aligned timeline without erasing their different channels.
options.viewport: The shared shell shows synchronized video frames, speech transcript, audio events, and sensor tracks in named lanes with aligned timestamps; non-temporal image and document workspaces remain separate task tools.
options.case: The score is powerful for audio/video/sensor alignment and annotation; it cannot be the dashboard's default for static images, documents, or tables.
options.risk: A temporal score only applies to some data; present it as a task-specific tool, never as the universal dataset model.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: One standard project dashboard with clear modality filters and a familiar table.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional sidebar, a modality filter row, a sortable dataset table with visible task/status fields, and a right-hand panel previewing the selected dataset and linking to its dedicated tool.
canonCard.risk: Highly familiar, but can feel like a generic file manager if modality-specific previews and meaningful next steps are missing.
